cases.sentence: На ___ простившись только с одним графом, не дождавшись выхода дам, князь Андрей поехал домой.
cases.explain: «другой день» — after the preposition «на», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: Next morning, having taken leave of no one but the count, and not waiting for the ladies to appear, Prince Andréy set off for home.

cases.sentence: ___ был жаркий, где-то собиралась гроза, но только небольшая тучка брызнула на пыль дороги и на сочные листья.
cases.explain: «Целый день» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: The whole day had been hot. Somewhere a storm was gathering, but only a small cloud had scattered some raindrops lightly, sprinkling the road and the sappy leaves. The left side of the forest was dark in the shade, the right side glittered in the sunlight, wet and shiny and scarcely swayed by the breeze. Everything was in blossom, the nightingales trilled, and their voices reverberated now near, now far away.

cases.sentence: ___ леса была темна, в тени; правая мокрая, глянцовитая блестела на солнце, чуть колыхаясь от ветра.
cases.explain: «Левая сторона» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.

cases.sentence: ___, весь преображенный, раскинувшись шатром сочной, темной зелени, млел, чуть колыхаясь в лучах вечернего солнца.
cases.explain: «Старый дуб» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Yes, here in this forest was that oak with which I agreed,” thought Prince Andréy. “But where is it?” he again wondered, gazing at the left side of the road, and without recognizing it he looked with admiration at the very oak he sought. The old oak, quite transfigured, spreading out a canopy of sappy dark-green foliage, stood rapt and slightly trembling in the rays of the evening sun. Neither gnarled fingers nor old scars nor old doubts and sorrows were any of them in evidence now. Through the hard century-old bark, even where there were no twigs, leaves had sprouted such as one could hardly believe the old veteran could have produced. “Yes, it is the same oak,” thought Prince Andréy, and all at once he was seized by an unreasoning springtime feeling of joy and renewal. All the best moments of his life suddenly rose to his memory. Austerlitz with the lofty heavens, his wife’s dead reproachful face, Pierre at the ferry, that girl thrilled by the beauty of the night, and that night itself and the moon, and … all this rushed suddenly to his mind.
